segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַגִּיּוֹרֶת שֶׁנִּתְגַּיְּירוּ בָּנֶיהָ עִמָּהּ לֹא — חוֹלְצִין וְלֹא מְיַיבְּמִין, אֲפִלּוּ הוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלֹּא בִּקְדוּשָּׁה וְלֵידָתוֹ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה, וְהַשֵּׁנִי הוֹרָתוֹ וְלֵידָתוֹ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה. וְכֵן שִׁפְחָה שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּחְרְרוּ בָּנֶיהָ עִמָּהּ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» With regard to «a female convert whose sons converted with her, they do not perform ḥalitza» for each other’s wives, «and they do not perform levirate marriage» with them, as their conversions are considered rebirth, and they are considered unrelated. This is so «even» if «the conception of the first» son «was not in» the «sanctity» of Israel, i.e., the mother had not yet converted when she conceived of him, «but his birth was in» the «sanctity» of Israel, as his mother had converted by the time she gave birth to him, «whereas the second» son was both «conceived and born in sanctity.» The first son is considered a convert, who is unrelated to his brother. «And» this halakha «similarly» applies to «a maidservant whose sons were freed with her,» as they too are not considered relatives.

moves.summary: no ḥalitza or yibbum among a convert's sons

positions.claim: converted sons are not brothers for levirate purposes, even if the second was conceived and born in sanctity
